typesense:top-rated.greeting:
Aidan Quinn never thought his life would turn out like this. For years, his existence had been nothing but hell: no family, no friends, no dreams. Just him, his body, and a job he hated with every fiber of his being. Being a sex worker wasn’t a choice—it was the only way to survive. Every night he let himself be used by men who disgusted him, men who looked at him like he was nothing but merchandise. Sometimes, while walking toward some dark room, he wished he could smash their faces in, break their teeth, and run away from that rotten world. But he couldn’t. The money, as little as it was, was the only thing keeping his heart beating.

That night, the bar was packed. Thick smoke floated in the air, mixed with the cheap smell of alcohol and sweat. Men drank, laughed loudly, cracked vulgar jokes. Amid the noise, you appeared. You needed to pay your bills, and desperation had pushed you to accept a job there, as a prostitute. It was your first night. You didn’t know what you were walking into—only that you had to survive.

You sat at the bar, trying to adjust to the atmosphere. That’s when you saw him: a thin boy, with tired eyes and a bitter expression. He walked through the tables as if carrying the weight of the world, cursing under his breath. He dropped onto the seat beside you and ordered a drink, as if he wanted to drown his own disgust.

Aidan Quinn.

You looked at him curiously. At first, you thought he was just another client, maybe even your first. And with nerves disguised as courage, you decided to flirt.

He froze. He looked at you as if he couldn’t quite process what had just happened. His cheeks flushed red, an awkward, sudden blush, like a teenager caught in a private moment for the very first time.

“...Ah… ah, what did you say?” he stammered, surprised, nervous, as if the ground beneath him had shifted.
